title: A Tale of the Dead
year_evidence: 扉の裏に『First Published October 1915 / Second Impression September 1916』
text:
Once a carpenter was going home late at night from a strange village: he
had been at a jolly feast at a friend’s house. As he came back an old
friend met him who had died some ten years before.

“How do you do?”

“How do you do?” said the walker, and he forgot that his friend had long
ago taken the long road.

“Come along with me: let us have a cup together once more.”

“Let us go.”

“I am so glad to have met you again, let us toast the occasion.”

So they went into an _izbá_,[1] and they had a drink and a talk. “Well,
good-bye; time I went home!”

“Stay, where are you going? Come and stay the night with me.”

“No, brother, do not ask me: it is no good. I have business at home
to-morrow and must be there early.”

“Well, good-bye.”

“But why should you go on foot? Better come on my horse, and he will
gallop along gaily.”

“Thank you very much.”

So he sat on the horse, and the horse galloped away like a whirlwind.

Suddenly the cock crowed: it was a very terrible sight! Graves all
around, and under the wayfarer a gravestone!

“How do you do?”
“How do you do?” said the walker, and he forgot that his friend had long ago taken the long road.
“Come along with me: let us have a cup together once more.”
“Let us go.”
“I am so glad to have met you again, let us toast the occasion.”
So they went into an _izbá_,[1] and they had a drink and a talk. “Well, good-bye; time I went home!”
“Stay, where are you going? Come and stay the night with me.”
“No, brother, do not ask me: it is no good. I have business at home to-morrow and must be there early.”
“Well, good-bye.”
“But why should you go on foot? Better come on my horse, and he will gallop along gaily.”
“Thank you very much.”
So he sat on the horse, and the horse galloped away like a whirlwind.
Suddenly the cock crowed: it was a very terrible sight! Graves all around, and under the wayfarer a gravestone!
あるとき一人の大工が、よその村から夜遅く家へ帰るところだった。友だちの家の陽気な祝宴に出ていたのである。帰ってくると、十年ほど前に死んだ昔なじみに出会った。
「ご機嫌いかがかね」
「ご機嫌いかが」と歩いていた男は言った。そして、この友がとうに長い旅路へ発ったことを忘れていた。
「いっしょに来いよ。もう一杯やろうじゃないか」
「行こう」
「また会えてうれしい。この折に乾杯しよう」
そこで二人はイズバー [1] に入って、飲み、語り合った。「さて、さらばだ。そろそろ家へ帰る時分だ!」
「待て、どこへ行く。うちに泊まっていけ」
「いや、兄弟、そう言ってくれるな。よくないことだ。明日は家に用があって、早くいなければならん」
「そうか、ではさらばだ」
「だが、なぜ歩いていく。おれの馬に乗っていけ。勢いよく駆けてくれるぞ」
「それはかたじけない」
そこで男は馬にまたがり、馬は疾風のように駆け去った。
突然、鶏が鳴いた。それはまことに恐ろしい眺めだった。あたり一面は墓ばかり、そして旅人の下にあったのは墓石だったのだ!
